title: Inventory counts differ
briefing: Storefront availability and warehouse records disagree for several products. Isolate the source of the discrepancy.

actions.label: Compare cache age with policy
actions.criteria: Use when edge entries are older than expected and expiry behavior has not been verified.
actions.instructions: Compare response age and the current expiry policy for affected products and warehouses.

actions.label: Inspect inventory namespace mapping
actions.criteria: Use when cache reads and inventory updates could use different namespaces for the same warehouse.
actions.instructions: Join read and update traces by warehouse and product, then compare the namespace fields.

actions.label: Inspect inventory event processing
actions.criteria: Use when inventory update events are absent or processing is delayed.
actions.instructions: Compare inventory message timestamps against update consumer lag and missing-event counters.

fallback: Capture a product and warehouse pair, then collect its inventory update and corresponding storefront response.

events.text: Inventory freshness SLO missed for 3% of responses. The alert does not list affected warehouses.
For SKU 301 at warehouse W7, the storefront is serving age=820 seconds from cache. Freshness for this response class is 120 seconds. Read namespace=stock-v1-W7.
The update for SKU 301 at W7 was accepted at 18:46 UTC. Write namespace=stock-v2-W7.
A second sample shows SKU 301 at W7 is still returning the cached response. The worker queue is within its lag objective.

debrief.summary: The writer had moved to the new namespace while the edge continued reading the old namespace. The cache age reflected that split.
lessons: Use the same warehouse and product identifiers when matching read and write records.
A normal consumer lag figure can coexist with stale data in a separate namespace.
